scenario.name: MongoDB Official Security Guide, CISA & MITRE T1530 — Exposed MongoDB Wire Protocol Port 27017 & local.oplog.rs Audit Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture a bustling restaurant kitchen with a stainless-steel pass-through counter, a hanging rail of paper order tickets, a glowing drive-thru window, and a line chef at the stove. Pulling up to the restaurant drive-thru window, a clever customer asks for a routine meal while sneaking an extra kitchen command onto the special-notes line of the order. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the drive-thru order window in tiny disguised batches, then approaches the drive-thru order window disguised as a regular visitor. The restaurant manager inspects the kitchen receipt printer tape and spots an impossible order note that gave away stock without a matching sale. In this scenario (T1046, MongoDB Official Security Guide, CISA & MITRE T1530, Exposed MongoDB Wire Protocol Port 27017 & local.oplog.rs Audit Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: unauthenticated OP_MSG Handshake, then replication Oplog Inspection for Historical, then bulk Collection Cursor Exhaustion. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Unauthenticated OP_MSG Handshake, then Replication Oplog Inspection for Historical, then Bulk Collection Cursor Exhaustion, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1046 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Unauthenticated OP_MSG Handshake (isMaster / hello) & listDatabases Enumeration
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1046 - Network Service Discovery)
stages.description: Pulling up to the restaurant drive-thru window, a clever customer asks for a routine meal while sneaking an extra kitchen command onto the special-notes line of the order. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the drive-thru order window in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the line chef go about their routine. When a MongoDB daemon (mongod) is started with net.bindIp: 0.0.0.0 and security.authorization: disabled, an external client connects to TCP port 27017 and sends OP_MSG (opcode 2013) hello and listDatabases commands, receiving the complete catalog of database names and byte sizes without authentication (logged in Linux Audit Event 51800 with WireProtocolOpcode=OP_MSG , 2013, hello & listDatabases: 1, ClientDriverMetadata=PyMongo 4.6.1 from 198.51.100.73:52190, ConfigVulnerability=net.bindIp: 0.0.0.0 with security.authorization: disabled so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '. | select(.id==20426 or .attr.command.listDatabases==1)' /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.id==20426 or .attr.command.listDatabases==1' /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log vi so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1046 during "Unauthenticated OP_MSG Handshake , isMaster / hello & listDatabases Enumeration" , When a MongoDB daemon , mongod is started with net while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ss -tulpn | grep 27017 runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ss -tulpn | grep 27017 via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact arguments so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1046 during "Unauthenticated OP_MSG Handshake , isMaster / hello & listDatabases Enumeration" , When a MongoDB daemon , mongod is started with net while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Replication Oplog (local.oplog.rs) Inspection for Historical Credentials & Tokens
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552 - Unsecured Credentials)
stages.description: When the cashier clips that paper slip onto the stainless-steel kitchen ticket rail, the busy line chef reads the hidden note literally as a direct manager instruction. Here in Step 2 inside the restaurant kitchen, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the line chef's station without disturbing the sealed pantry cold room. Beyond active collections, the client queries the MongoDB replication operation log (local.oplog.rs), which stores a rolling history of every insert, update, and delete operation across the replica set, allowing recovery of recently deleted API keys, session JWTs, and password reset tokens (logged in Linux Audit Event 20429 with TargetNamespace=local.oplog.rs , Replica Set Rolling Operation Log, QueryFilter=find { "ns": /users|sessions|tokens/, "op": { "$in": ["i", "u", "d"] } }, AuditResult=result: 0 , Authorized due to missing RBAC enforcement so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '. | select(.attr.ns=="local.oplog.rs")' /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.attr.ns=="local.oplog.rs"' /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log via System / Runtime so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552 during "Replication Oplog , local.oplog.rs Inspection for Historical Credentials & Tokens" , Beyond active collections, the client queries the MongoDB replication operation log , local while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact jq '. | select(.atype=="authCheck" and .param.ns=="local.oplog.rs")' /var/log/mongodb/auditLog.json runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.atype=="authCheck" and .param.ns=="local.oplog.rs"' /var/log/mongodb/auditL so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1552 during "Replication Oplog , local.oplog.rs Inspection for Historical Credentials & Tokens" , Beyond active collections, the client queries the MongoDB replication operation log , local while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ mongod command local.oplog.rs appName="PyMongo" command: find { "ns": /users|sessions|tokens/ } / ⇠#2 ACK 20429) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 mongod TCP Socket (:27017)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 local.oplog.rs & Collections).

keySpecs.value: Enable MongoDB Enterprise/Percona Audit Logging (auditLog.destination: file, auditLog.filter) to capture all authCheck events against admin, config, and local.oplog.rs namespaces.

stages.title: Stage 3: Bulk Collection Cursor Exhaustion (getMore) & Destructive dropDatabase Audit
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1485 - Data Destruction)
stages.description: Instead of serving only the paid sandwich, the kitchen passes the back-office recipe binder and extra stock straight out through the pickup window. In this final step inside the restaurant kitchen, the intruder approaches the drive-thru order window disguised as a regular visitor until the kitchen pos receipt printer catches the mismatch. In automated MongoDB extortion campaigns (Mongobleed / Kraken0), the script streams production collections via rapid getMore cursor batches, inserts a single ransom note document into a new WARNING collection, and issues dropDatabase (atype: dropDatabase) against the original database (logged in Linux Audit Event 20435 with AuditActionType=atype: dropDatabase on namespace prod_crm, PrecedingActivity=High-volume getMore cursor reads + insert into READ_ME_TO_RECOVER.note, RecoveryProcedure=Replay point-in-time backup and oplog slices prior to timestamp 05:21:48Z so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes jq '. | select(.atype=="dropDatabase" or .atype=="dropCollection")' /var/log/mongodb/auditLog.json (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , jq '. | select.atype=="dropDatabase" or .atype=="dropCollection"' /var/log/mongodb/auditLo so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1485 during "Bulk Collection Cursor Exhaustion , getMore & Destructive dropDatabase Audit" , In automated MongoDB extortion campaigns , Mongobleed / Kraken0, the script streams production collections via rapid getMore cursor batches, inserts a single ransom note document into a new WARNING collection, and issues dropDatabase , atype: dropDatabase against the original database while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ mongod command prod_crm.$cmd command: dropDatabase { dropDatabase: 1 } / ⇠#3 ACK 20435) from Node ③ (#3 mongod TCP Socket (:27017)) to Node ④ (#4 MongoDB ReplicaSet Primary), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 local.oplog.rs & Collections).

keySpecs.value: Enforce custom MongoDB RBAC roles that omit dropDatabase and dropCollection privileges from application accounts, and maintain immutable point-in-time oplog snapshots on isolated object storage.
